Subject: Medscribe — post-demo recap & long-context eval plan

Claire — great demo earlier, thanks for the walkthrough. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary of needs we captured
- Primary: accurate, extractive-style summaries of long clinical encounter notes (20–50k tokens) with strong fidelity to patient facts and no hallucinated clinical assertions.
- Secondary: fast retrieval-friendly summaries (brief TL;DR + structured key findings).
- Constraints: PHI-sensitive; on-prem/private deployment required for production.

Preliminary model fit suggestions (based on today's sample doc and latency/cost targets):
- Redwood-70B-extended-q4 (64k window) — best starting point for high-fidelity summarization at scale.
- Redwood-13B-extended — lower-cost routing for short encounters and iterative drafts.
- Fallback: scheduled cascade to smaller quantized variant for low-priority batching.

Attachments I attached to this thread: medscribe_prompt_set_v2.csv (sample prompts + temperature sweep), medscribe_longdoc_bench_v1.pdf (initial synthetic benchmark results), redwood_security_qs_response.docx (SOC/KMS notes).

Concerns to flag internally: we observed some truncation artifacts in our early 32k baseline that changed how clinical timelines were represented. We need a focused eval that measures "timeline preservation" and "reference_preservation" rather than just ROUGE.

Proposed next steps (ask):
1) MedScribe: share 3–5 representative long notes (anonymized) and highlight the one example you want prioritized. procurement@medscribe.ai indicated legal review — happy to accommodate an NDA if needed.
2) Redwood: we will run a 64k-focused eval (compare Redwood-70B-extended-q4 and 13B-extended) and return a short report with summary fidelity metrics + sample outputs by EOD Friday (11/12).
3) Schedule: 30-min follow-up to review results and pick an integration approach.

If that timeline works I’ll kick off internal ops + sign-off. Thanks again — excited about this.

—

Jordan/Neha — quick technical plan and what I need from the customer: 

Eval plan (high level)- Create an eval harness that runs both models on the supplied docs, capturing:
  * token-level truncation points (where model drops context)
  * timeline_preservation score (custom: percentage of events in correct temporal order vs annotated refs)
  * reference_preservation score (factual span overlap for key fields)
  * hallucination_rate (clinically relevant false assertions flagged)

- Generation regime: deterministic sampling (temp 0.0) + a calibrated beam/beamless pass for extraction tasks.
- Prompt ensembles: we’ll evaluate the prompt set Claire sent (medscribe_prompt_set_v2.csv) plus two difference-instruction variants (short-structured + narrative-first).

Compute estimate and deliverable- For three ~40k-token docs on 70B-ext-q4: ~6 GPU-hours total (batching + KV reuse) across optimized runtime; estimate ~ $900 in marginal cloud compute on hosted profile.
- 13B-ext runs roughly 1/4 the cost and can be used to sanity-check outputs and propose cost-optimized routing.

Risks / regression observations- On our older 32k baseline we saw summary condensation that collapsed temporally adjacent events (likely a positional/attention truncation artifact). We need to ensure positional embeddings and KV cache handling are validated in the 64k path.

What I need from the customer- Confirm delivery of 3 anonymized notes + a one-paragraph annotation for the event timeline that matters most in each doc.
- Point of contact for security questions (I’ll use the redwood_security_qs_response.docx to accelerate).

I’ll spin up the harness tonight and expect a first-pass PDF report by EOD 11/12. If the customer wants we can add a short video walkthrough.
